To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
negative entities do not exist and that negative findings can be accommodated in an ontologically realist EHR.

the referent tracking approach can accommodate negative findings, but only by means of an ontological relation between a particular and an universal that we have called 'non-qualified ontological relation'.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a problem which has not previously been addressed in the literature.
the question of how to deal with negative entities in a referent tracking based Electronic Health Record.
the ontological status of negative findings in an electronic health record.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
referent tracking is able to deal with negative findings in a way that does not involve negative entities.
the paradigm of referent-tracking, as it stands, can accommodate negative findings in the sense of negative findings in a medical context.
referent tracking, in its current form, is able to accommodate all the negative findings in the sample examined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
referent tracking is not just a useful tool for dealing with the ontological problems of the Electronic Health Record; it is a tool which can be used to solve ontological problems in general.
referent tracking is not as problematic as some have suggested, and that the problem of negative findings can be resolved in a referent tracking context without recourse to a negative entities.

the problem of negative findings is solved by a realist ontology which does not allow negative entities, but does allow a particular to have a relation to a universal which does not hold for any other particular.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the paradigm of referent-tracking is not as restricted as it has been thought to be.
a referent tracking ontology, which rejects negative entities, is able to deal with negative findings in ways that are consistent with its basic realist commitments.
the problem of negative findings is not an insurmountable obstacle to a referent tracking based approach to EHRs.
